subject: Request: model-binding waiver and no-fallback runway for Medvy EU pilot
messages:
From: Diana Flores <diana@medvy.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge@medvy.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot constraints: EU-only + deterministic model binding request

Hi Markus —

Quick context: Medvy is starting a six-week EU pilot for our clinical transcription feature. Our legal and customers require both data residency and deterministic inference for specific workflows. That means we can’t fall back to a different model variant mid-request — variation in tokenization/quantization changes downstream annotations.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a short-term waiver to pin us to the selected EU-hosted model (no automatic fallback to alternate variants) for the pilot window?
- We’ll need an ops/playbook that describes the runway for exception removal (how long a waiver can run, rollback steps if capacity issues occur).

Attached are our residency requirements and a short note on determinism. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Diana Flores
Head of Product, Medvy Health

Attachments: medvy_eu_residency_requirements.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Diana Flores <diana@medvy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot constraints: EU-only + deterministic model binding request

Diana — thanks for the clear ask and the docs. Looping product, infra and security to scope. High-level notes from me:

- We can create a region-locked deployment (EU) and pin the model variant for a given customer routing policy.
- The primary concern is resilience: our runtime currently supports fallbacks to keep latency/availability SLOs during node failures. Removing fallback increases outage risk and complicates autoscaling.

Marissa / Karthik / Irene — can you confirm the minimum technical caveats we should present to Medvy and propose a runway plan? Specifically:
  1) Max waiver duration we can realistically support without a formal capacity commitment.
  2) Ops steps if pinned model becomes unhealthy (automated alerts, manual override process).
  3) Any compliance gaps (audit log, KMS separation) we need for an exception.

I’ll coordinate a cross-functional sync tomorrow; tentative agenda attached.

— Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: waiver_runway_draft.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Diana Flores <diana@medvy.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot constraints: EU-only + deterministic model binding request

Thanks Markus & Diana — product perspective below. I prioritized the practical constraints so we can present clear options to Medvy: 

Summary: We can support a time-limited model-binding waiver for a pilot if Medvy accepts one of two paths.

Option A — Short runway (recommended for pilots):
- Duration: up to 8 weeks with automated monitoring + daily ops check-ins.
- Constraints: waiver only for non-production traffic patterns (pilot traffic volumes). If pilot grows beyond set TPS thresholds we require a capacity commitment or falling back becomes mandatory.
- Rollback: ops triggers a forced switch to a compatible fallback variant after a 15-minute incident window; customers are notified by email.

Option B — Committed capacity (for production readiness):
- Duration: contractually-backed (quarterly minimum).
- Constraints: Dedicated capacity in EU pool, prioritized scheduling, and SLA for availability.

Technical notes for Karthik: we’ll need a per-tenant route flag (no_fallback=true) and a safety timeout that still lets the system fail open for catastrophic node-level issues (e.g., whole Availability Zone failure).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: short note on implementation complexity and estimated ETA.
- Irene: list of specific audit/KMS items we must certify for the waiver.
- Markus/Diana: confirm pilot traffic expectations (TPS, burst patterns).

— Marissa
Senior PM, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Diana Flores <diana@medvy.com>
Date: 2028-08-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot constraints: EU-only + deterministic model binding request

Quick security/compliance input:

- Residency: EU-hosted inference + customer-managed KMS (recommended). Medvy will need proof of separation for key material; we can provide a KMS integration guide.
- Auditability: every inference request under the waiver must be logged with model-version metadata, route flags, and the waiver ID. These logs must be retained for 1 year in the EU region.
- Emergency fallback: from a compliance perspective, we can allow an emergency, documented fallback only if it is:
   a) pre-authorized by Medvy (written acceptance in the waiver), and
   b) recorded with timestamp + incident report to both Medvy and Redwood’s compliance logs.

Attached is our security checklist that maps to the waiver items. Please review the KMS and logging asks — they are non-negotiable for the compliance team.

—Irene
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: security_checklist_v2.docx
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Diana Flores <diana@medvy.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot constraints: EU-only + deterministic model binding request

Thanks all — summary & action items for the Medvy pilot waiver:

1) We will offer a time-limited, EU-only model-binding waiver for the six-week pilot with the following hard constraints:
   - Trial duration: 6 weeks (start date TBD by Medvy).
   - No automatic fallback allowed during normal operation; emergency fallback allowed only under the compliance emergency process Irene outlined.
   - Medvy to accept retention and logging commitments (1 year) and to enable customer-managed KMS.

2) Technical implementation (Karthik):
   - Add per-tenant flag no_fallback=true; ETA: ~3 weeks for a guarded rollout to canary, 1 week of canary verification.
   - Implement alerting + auto-notification hooks for ops.

3) Product/Commercial (Marissa & Markus):
   - Offer Option A (8-week pilot runway) as baseline; provide conversion path to committed capacity if traffic > threshold.
   - Update the pilot SOW with the waiver language and emergency fallback acceptance clause.

4) Compliance (Irene):
   - Deliver KMS integration guide and log schema by EOD 2028-08-14.

5) Admin: I opened JIRA INF-3247 and created a Confluence page for the waiver doc.

Marissa/Karthik/Irene — if you can confirm the dates above and ETA items by EOD tomorrow I will send a consolidated waiver draft to Medvy and request their signature.

Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Related links: JIRA INF-3247, Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/medvy-eu-waiver
